text:
Alex (People Ops): Quick question to the channel — we had a payroll vendor cutover this morning and Dana says she changed her 401(k) election mid-cycle. Can payroll/vendor confirm how mid-pay elections were handled?
Dana L.: I switched from pre-tax -> Roth for my regular deferral and checked the "50+ catch-up" box in the new portal. Did that get recorded? I'm worried catch-up defaulting to pre-tax. Also I have an open 401k loan — will repayments continue the same?
Rob (Payroll): Hi @Alex, @Dana L. — vendor cutover ran at 02:00 PDT. During cutover we freeze election imports for the current pay cycle. Our standard behavior: changes submitted after the vendor cutoff are queued and start next pay period.
Caroline - Benefits: From PensionCo side: we received two files yesterday and a final snapshot at cutover. Catch-up designation is a separate field — if it's present in the submission we honor it; if absent we map to the participant's prior designation, otherwise plan default is pre-tax.
Dana L.: I definitely clicked Roth for both regular and catch-up in the new UI. I also uploaded the signed catch-up attestation PDF.
Rob (Payroll): Can you DM me the confirmation receipt number? I can check whether the submission made it into the pre-cutover snapshot.
Dana L.: Receipt #2078-CCK. Sent in DM.
Erin F.: Note for records: if the catch-up was incorrectly posted as pre-tax we need to fix it before year-end to avoid tax issues. There is a window for corrective reclassifications but it's better to catch now.
BenefitsBot: Automated import log: 
```
2078900001 - initial snapshot imported
2078903600 - supplemental elections file received
2078907200 - final snapshot (cutover) received
2078909000 - post-cutover delta file rejected (system freeze)
```
Caroline - Benefits: Based on the log, the post-cutover delta was rejected — that means any changes Dana made after the final snapshot did not land. Rob, do you have the exact boundary time?
Rob (Payroll): Cutover final snapshot timestamp: 2078907200 (02:00 PDT). Any submissions after that were processed for the next payroll.
Alex (People Ops): Two action items: (1) Rob, can you check whether Receipt #2078-CCK appears in the final snapshot on your side? (2) Caroline, if it didn't, can PensionCo do a manual intake for this catch-up designation and backdate the election to this cycle if possible? We want to avoid a mis-posting for Dana.
Rob (Payroll): I found the receipt in the supplemental file at 2078903500 — it should have been in the final snapshot. Will open a ticket with payroll ops to confirm why it wasn't included in the final export.
Caroline - Benefits: If it's present in our supplemental we can accept a manual correction form. However plan rules: elective deferral type changes are effective the pay period identified, subject to payroll processing. For loan repayments: those continue unchanged; loans are handled outside the deferral election stream.
Dana L.: Phew. If it helps, I can re-submit through the old vendor portal too. But I wanted to avoid duplicate submissions.
Erin F.: Finance note: if a reclassification is required for the tax year, we'll need proper audit trail + signed participant election. Keep all receipts.
Alex (People Ops): I'll coordinate with Payroll and Benefits. Expected next steps: Rob to confirm inclusion in final snapshot (ETA 2h), Caroline to confirm if PensionCo can accept manual correction and whether they can backdate for this pay period (ETA 4h). Dana: hold off on resubmitting until we confirm to avoid duplicates.
Rob (Payroll): Confirmed — ticket created (#PR-4592). I'll post updates here when we hear back.
Caroline - Benefits: If we need to backdate a Roth catch-up, we'll require the signed attestation + the confirmation number. We can process a reclassification within 5 business days if payroll provides the paydate and amount.
BenefitsBot: Ticket created in Benefits queue: BENE-2183 linking PR-4592.
Dana L.: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick help. :heart:
Alex (People Ops): Thanks @Rob, @Caroline. I'll follow up once both tickets have resolution and update the payroll FAQ with the cutover cutoff times so folks know.
Rob (Payroll): One quick FYI for the FAQ draft — cutover boundary = final snapshot (export) time, not portal submission time. We'll share exact UTC/PDT times.
Erin F.: Also adding a short blurb about catch-up defaulting rules for employees 50+.
Alex (People Ops): Closing loop: we'll keep thread open until PensionCo confirms whether they can backdate and Payroll confirms the original submission made it into final snapshot.
Caroline - Benefits: Will update before EOD.
Rob (Payroll): Will update within 2h.
BenefitsBot: Update logged 2078901402: BENE-2183 assigned to Caroline; PR-4592 status = investigating.
